title: Greywater Bay Rising Again
premise: When a confession letter arrives at Greywater Bay's coroner's office postmarked the day after old fisherman Amos Delacroix's funeral, Silas Joubert realizes the letter names him as the keeper of evidence he buried twenty years ago — a drowned girl ruled accidental, whose file he quietly altered to protect someone he loved. As more letters arrive, each quoting details only the original investigators knew, Silas must reconstruct his own compromised memory of that summer while pretending to run an honest investigation. The letter-writer is Amos himself, who staged his death and is watching from the marshes, testing whether Silas will finally choose truth over loyalty. In the climax, Silas lures Amos back to the bay with a public exhumation order, confronts him in the flooded church where the girl died, and chooses to file the true report — burning his twenty years of careful lies and turning himself in alongside the man who orchestrated it all.
about_author: Theo Okafor spent a decade as a records clerk in coastal Louisiana parish offices before turning to fiction, a job that taught him how much truth lives in filing cabinets. He writes mysteries about small towns where the archives are the real crime scenes.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Silas Joubert files his two-thousandth death certificate, then opens a confession letter for a drowning ruled accidental twenty years ago. The handwriting belongs to Amos Delacroix, buried last week. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in professional calm — the past has learned to write.

chapters.title: The Alphabetical Dead
chapters.summary: Silas rereads the sealed 2004 case file and finds his own forged notation staring back at him. A second letter arrives quoting a detail never written down — only witnessed. POV: Silas, with flashbacks to young deputy Silas. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into fear as memory proves unreliable.

chapters.title: What the Marsh Keeps
chapters.summary: Silas visits the Delacroix family under pretense of routine follow-up; Amos's granddaughter Odile mentions her grandfather mailed something the day before he 'died.' POV: Odile. Emotional beat: she suspects the funeral was theater and resents being kept outside every family secret.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: A flashback-heavy chapter: young Silas alters the report to protect his mentor, Sheriff Broussard, whose son was on the boat that night. POV: alternating past and present Silas. Emotional beat: the slow corrosion of a good man's compromise.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: A third letter includes a photograph of a second body — a drifter who vanished the same week in 2004, never investigated. Silas realizes the case is bigger than one drowning. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: vertigo; the file he thought he knew contains rooms he never entered.

chapters.title: Broussard's Silence
chapters.summary: Silas confronts the retired sheriff, now dying of emphysema, who neither confirms nor denies but warns him to let the dead stay filed. That night Silas's office is searched. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: loyalty and self-preservation pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Odile's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Odile finds Amos's hidden journals showing he witnessed everything from the water that night — including young Silas's arrival afterward. She must decide whether to help the man who helped bury the truth. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: fury curdling into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Exhumation Order
chapters.summary: Silas plays his only card: publicly ordering Amos's exhumation, betting the letter-writer cannot resist watching. Odile helps him stage the announcement. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cold clarity — he stops running from the trap and starts setting his own.

chapters.title: The Flooded Church
chapters.summary: Amos appears at the half-drowned chapel where Céleste died; alive, gaunt, having faked his death to force a reckoning no court would allow. He demands Silas confess aloud what he filed away. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the confrontation he has dodged for twenty years, arriving all at once.

chapters.title: Filed Under Truth
chapters.summary: Silas signs the corrected reports naming Broussard's son, then adds his own falsification charge — and Amos turns himself in for the drifter's death. Odile publishes the journals. POV: Silas, closing with Odile. Emotional beat: grief without absolution, but the archive is finally honest.
